question: According to DSM-5, a child who meets full diagnostic criteria for both ADHD and Autism Spectrum Disorder should receive both diagnoses simultaneously.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is actually TRUE. DSM-IV precluded an ADHD diagnosis if ASD was present; DSM-5 reversed this. Dual diagnosis is now encouraged when both condition criteria are independently met, as it guides more comprehensive treatment planning.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. DSM-5 removed the previous exclusion that prevented dual diagnosis. Co-occurring ADHD and ASD is not only permitted but is common — approximately 30–50% of children with ASD also meet ADHD criteria.
